Fix: use a parameterized query, e.g. `db.QueryContext(ctx, \"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name LIKE ?\", \"%\"+escapeLike(q)+\"%\")` (use `$1` on Postgres). Escape `%`/`_` in `q` so users can't force expensive wildcard scans. Also cap `q` length and add LIMIT/pagination, and make sure the SELECT returns only non-sensitive columns (no password hashes or tokens).
